subject: Forensic preservation: scope, evidentiary deliverables, and approval flow
messages:
From: Timothy Lane <timothy.lane@medproof.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.example
Cc: security@medsecure.io
Date: 2026-07-12T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary forensic preservation for tenant 'mp-tenant-3'

Hi Alex,

We have an active internal investigation and need Redwood to preserve detailed request/response logs and audit trails for tenant 'mp-tenant-3' starting 2026-06-01 through present. Our standard SOC 2 auditors are asking for an unbroken chain of custody and signed attestation that these logs will not be purged for at least 180 days while we complete the review.

Deliverables requested by our legal team:
- Full (non-sampled) export of audit logs and request traces for tenant mp-tenant-3 (JSON or Parquet)
- A signed attestation from Redwood confirming the hold window and access restrictions
- Evidence of export (S3 link + checksums) and a short manifest describing schema and redaction policy

Please let me know what you can provide, expected timelines, and any additional internal approvals you will need. If you prefer a short call to align, I can do 2pm PT today.

Thanks,
Tim
Timothy Lane
Security Ops, MedProof Labs
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example>
To: Timothy Lane <timothy.lane@medproof.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.example, priyom_das@redwood.example
Date: 2026-07-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary forensic preservation for tenant 'mp-tenant-3'

Tim —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can support a scoped forensic preservation, but this requires a short approval flow (Security -> Legal -> Product Ops) and a signed justification document from MedProof confirming the legal hold trigger.

High-level constraints and what we can deliver:
- Standard retention: ephemeral session logs (30 days), request traces and audit logs (90 days). An exception can extend to a temporary hold (configurable up to 365 days) if approved.
- Export formats: NDJSON, Parquet. We can deliver S3 export plus a manifest and SHA256 checksums.
- PII/redaction: we can produce both raw and redacted exports (redaction rules will be documented).
- Access controls: exports will be stored in a scoped S3 bucket, encrypted with customer-managed KMS (if provided), and access limited to list of named roles.

I've attached a preliminary forensic_evidence_checklist.xlsx (attachment) that lists the fields we typically provide and the decisions required from you (raw vs redacted, exact time window, required retention length).

Next steps I need from you:
1) Confirm exact tenant id(s) and earliest timestamp to preserve.
2) Confirm requested hold window (days).
3) Upload a signed legal hold notice and identify MedProof point of contact for attestations.

CC'ing Priyom for technical scope and Grace for compliance sign-off routing. If you want the 2pm PT call we can do it — Jon and I are available.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: forensic_evidence_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-07-13T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: temporary forensic preservation for tenant 'mp-tenant-3' — technical export options

Alex / Grace —

Quick technical summary for what Ops can produce and implementation notes: 
- Export contents: request_id, timestamp (ISO8601), model_name, prompt_hash, response_hash, request_headers (redacted), response_length_tokens, request_latency_ms, route_id, node_id, and audit_event (user / admin actions).
- Format & delivery: we will generate Parquet + manifest.json with column-level checksums. Delivery options: pre-signed S3 link (7-day expiry) or upload to a customer-owned S3 (preferred for long holds).
- Redaction: we can run a deterministic PII redaction pass; redaction will be reversible only if you provide salt/key for reversible masking. Otherwise we will do non-reversible token-level redaction and include a mapping summary.
- Ephemeral caches and KV: NOTE — runtime KV cache is ephemeral and not persisted to disk; it is not part of exports. Session-level ephemeral traces are aggregated and may be sampled if the retention window pre-dates persistence policies. We'll mark any sampled ranges in the manifest.
- Estimated ops work: 1 business day to scope and validate, 2–3 business days to produce full export for a 3-month window (depends on token volume).

I recommend the following default: produce a raw export to a scoped customer S3 bucket, plus a redacted export with PII removed. For SOC 2 evidence, include the manifest, checksums, and a simple access log showing who accessed the export.

Happy to join the call to walk through the technical checklist.

Thanks,
Priyom (Infra / Runtime)
From: Legal Ops <legal@medproof.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example>
Cc: security@medsecure.io, grace_oconnor@redwood.example
Date: 2026-07-15T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: MedProof legal hold confirmation + 180-day preservation request

Alex —

On behalf of MedProof Labs legal, we are confirming a formal legal hold tied to investigation MP-INV-2026-17. We request Redwood preserve the specified logs for 180 days from 2026-07-15 (i.e., through 2027-01-11). This is a firm request unless Redwood requires a more narrow scope; please advise ASAP if 180 days is not feasible.

Attached is our signed-hold.pdf (attachment). Please provide:
- A signed attestation template from Redwood confirming preservation scope and access controls
- CAIQ/SIG mapping for controls relevant to forensic evidence retention (we need the control IDs used by your team for audit traces and log retention)

If you need the legal hold to be narrower (specific datasets or date ranges), propose your recommended scoping and confirm any cost implications.

Regards,
Maya Cohen
Legal Counsel, MedProof Labs

Attachment: signed-hold.pdf (PDF stub)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-07-16T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: approval flow & controls for MedProof hold

Team —

Quick internal note on approvals and mitigations for a 180-day preservation: 
- Required approvals: Security (Grace) -> Legal (Alex to collect signed hold) -> Product Ops (Jonas) -> Engineering (Priyom) for export production.
- Operational mitigations: export to a dedicated bucket with CMEK, retention lock applied for the requested window, narrow ACLs, and audit logging of export access.
- Cost/impact: estimated storage increase ~ 600GB (depends on token volume). We should surface cost to customer unless Legal asks us to absorb it.
- Controls evidence we'll attach to attestation: storage encryption logs, access audit trail (who downloaded the S3 object), manifest checksums, and export job runbook.

I'm attaching a quick approval-flow-diagram.png (attachment) to include in the attestation packet. Once Grace gives compliance sign-off I can raise the ops ticket and schedule the export.

Jonas
Director, Product Ops
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example>
To: Timothy Lane <timothy.lane@medproof.com>, Maya Cohen <legal@medproof.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.example, priyom_das@redwood.example, jonas_weber@redwood.example
Date: 2026-07-19T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Forensic preservation: scope, evidentiary deliverables, and approval flow — confirmed deliverables & timeline

Thanks all — finalizing scope and timeline below. Per MedProof's signed hold we've approved a scoped preservation for tenant mp-tenant-3 with the following deliverables and schedule: 

1) Deliverables
  - Full Parquet export (raw) covering 2026-06-01 -> present. File manifest + SHA256 checksums.
  - Redacted export (non-reversible PII removal) and a redaction summary.
  - Signed Redwood attestation PDF confirming hold start 2026-07-15, retention until 2027-01-11, access controls, and encryption details.
  - Access audit log showing download events for the export objects.
  - Operational runbook (short doc) describing export job and retention lock steps.

2) Timeline
  - Ops scoping & validation: 2 business days (complete by 2026-07-21).
  - Export generation and delivery to customer S3: estimated 3 business days after validation (target delivery 2026-07-26).
  - Attestation and compliance packet (signed-approval.pdf) to follow within 48 hours of export delivery.

3) Next actions for MedProof
  - Confirm you accept the 180-day window and the scope above.
  - Confirm destination (Redwood-scoped S3 vs customer-owned S3). If customer-owned, provide bucket name and KMS key ARN.
  - Identify the list of people allowed to access the export.

For CAIQ/SIG mapping: Grace will produce a short mapping document that points to the controls we rely on for ingestion, logging, and retention; that will be bundled with the attestation.

If anything needs to be more narrow (specific dates or event types) please reply with exact filter criteria. Otherwise we will kick off ops on Monday.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: signed-approval.pdf (PDF stub)
